findings.description: The documented library-setup step says to disable the remote metadata/image fetchers but does not state that SaveLocalMetadata must remain disabled. Enabling SaveLocalMetadata=true makes Jellyfin's own local image saver rewrite the media folder (the badge is written as folder.png/-thumb.png and the original poster.jpg/S01E01.jpg sidecars are removed), which invalidates the source-preservation check. This is host behavior, not ArrTags behavior; the ArrTags SourceArtifactId still recorded the original poster hash at capture time.
evidence: With SaveLocalMetadata=true: movie folder gained folder.png (7,952 bytes = the published badge) and backdrop.jpg, and poster.jpg was removed; the episode folder gained ArrTagsTestShow.S01E01-thumb.png (6,626 bytes = the published badge) and S01E01.jpg was removed.
With SaveLocalMetadata=false: poster.jpg, S01E01.jpg and all three .nfo files were byte-identical before and after publication.
findings.recommended_action: Add an explicit note to docs/testing/jellyfin-12-musl-test-host.md that SaveLocalMetadata must stay false for the source-preservation check.

findings.description: After a full library scan re-adopted the local sidecar poster as the item Primary image, ArrTags observed the changed active-image identity, transitioned the artwork-state to OwnershipLost (State=2), and (by design) blocked automatic publication, so subsequent reconciliations did not re-assert the badge. This is the documented fail-closed decision (docs/data-model.md 3.10.4; docs/architecture.md lines 847-937); it is not a defect.
evidence: artwork-state movie State=2, LastOwnershipObservation {Status:1, Reason:'The active image content hash changed.', Observed.ContentSha256:93237BC3...}
ArtworkRegenerationPlanner.IsPublicationBlocked returns true for OwnershipLost and the planner then Skips.
docs/data-model.md: 'Published' + current identity differs -> OwnershipLost -> 'Do not publish, restore, or remove automatically.'
findings.recommended_action: None required; the behavior is intentional. An operator would start a new session through an explicit administrative action.
